- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model often lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.3–0.6), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average to reduce noise.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often forecasts too low; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
